Developers: embed, automate, get notified#

Everything a developer needs to put Verse scenes in their own product, in copy-paste form:

  1. <verse-viewer> — one tag on any page.
  2. React and Vue — thin typed wrappers over that tag.
  3. The REST SDK — upload, wait, publish, private links, embed code, analytics.
  4. Webhooks — scene.ready / scene.failed, signed and retried.
  5. MCP server (unreleased) — let AI assistants and agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) upload a 3D file and hand back a Verse link.

Start at the developer hub: a live demo with copy-paste code for HTML, React, Vue, Node and curl, and a playground where you paste a GLB link or drop a small file and get a live preview, the embed code and an SDK snippet. Runnable examples (Next.js, Vite + React, Vue, plain HTML, a Shopify product page, a Node upload script and a webhook receiver) live in sdk/public-examples/; designer tools (Framer, Webflow, Figma) in integrations/designers/ (guide).

Install: npm install @ctruhtech/verse-sdk @ctruhtech/verse-viewer @ctruhtech/verse-react @ctruhtech/verse-vue (take what you need). Each package has a 60-second quickstart in its README.

Replace https://verse.ctruh.com with your Verse origin if you run your own. The account token is the credential — create one in Studio (/studio) or with POST /v1/account; keep it server-side.

Reference: api.md (every route), sdk.md (every SDK method), embed-sdk.md (every viewer verb and event). Postman: web/playground/verse-api.postman_collection.json.

Adoption numbers#

/developers/adoption is a public page of aggregate counts, fed by GET /v1/adoption (JSON, cached five minutes): weekly npm downloads for @ctruhtech/* and the SDK repository's GitHub stars (both fetched by the server and cached an hour), and from the server itself: API keys used in the last 30 days (a count), distinct sites embedding Verse, scenes served per week, and MCP calls. No personal data: a site is kept only as a salted one-way hash, so there is no list, no IP address and no page path.

  • Being listed. A scene owner can opt in with POST /v1/adoption/optin {"listDomains": true} (Bearer token); the sites that embed their scenes are then named on the page. false withdraws and deletes the stored names. GET on the same route reads the setting.
  • MCP counter. The MCP server reports each tool call with POST /v1/mcp/ping {"tool": "upload_scene"} (any account token or org key). Only a short tool label is kept.

<verse-viewer>#

Code
<script src="https://verse.ctruh.com/embed.js" async></script>

<verse-viewer
  src="palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
  poster="https://verse.ctruh.com/ingest/palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f.poster.png"
  autoplay-tour>
</verse-viewer>

That is the whole integration. The 3D engine runs in an iframe from the Verse origin, so your page needs no special headers; the element is lazy (no frame, no engine bytes until it comes within 300 px of the viewport), responsive (100 % of its container's width at 16:9), and keeps the embed scroll guard — on a phone a vertical swipe over the scene scrolls your page until the visitor taps into the scene; the mouse wheel does the same on desktop.

Attributes#

AttributeValue
srcscene id · .vpk / .glb / .fidelity.glb URL · a share linkrequired; a share link's share, look, bg and variant come along
share32-hex share tokenopens a private scene (private links)
posterimage URLshown until the scene draws (and if 3D cannot start)
backgroundrrggbb · transparent · grad:a,b · studio:neutral|warm|dark · image:… · hdr:…changes live
looklook preset, e.g. studio:warm, showroom
loadlazy (default) · eager · taptap shows a "View in 3D" button and loads nothing until it is pressed
autoplay-tourbooleanplays the owner's guided tour once the scene is in
aspect16:9 (default) · 4:3 · 1:1 · 3:4 · 9:16 · 21:9 · fillfill = the element's own CSS height
tiera · cpin the renderer: WebGPU where available (default) or WebGL2
hotspots · guard · fullscreen · analyticsfalse to turn offpins + tour · scroll guard · fullscreen button · view analytics
variant · qualitymaterial variant name · 4k

Changing an attribute re-mounts the viewer (except background, which changes in place).

Events#

DOM CustomEvents on the element; the payload is event.detail.

Eventdetail
load{ name, clusters?, streamed?, animations? } — the scene is in (streamed scenes keep refining)
ready{ tier, ttfi } — the engine booted (tier "A/B" WebGPU or "C" WebGL2)
progress{ drawn, total, fraction } — ~1 Hz streaming progress
error{ message, code? } — code: "degraded" when 3D cannot start here (the poster stays), "no-source" without src
hotspot{ id, label?, title? } — a hotspot was visited (click, tour, or viewer.goTo)
view-change{ position: [x,y,z], forward: [x,y,z] } — the camera moved (≤ 4 Hz, world metres)
tour{ playing, steps?, seconds? }

Every other viewer event (stage, variant, measure, …) is dispatched under its own name too.

Methods#

Code
const el = document.querySelector("verse-viewer");
el.addEventListener("load", () => console.log("in"));
el.addEventListener("view-change", (e) => console.log(e.detail.position));

await el.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] }); // orbit camera: eye + pivot
await el.playTour();                                             // the owner's guided tour
el.stopTour();
const png = await el.screenshot();                               // Blob (image/png) of the current frame
el.activate();                                                   // mount now (skip lazy / tap)
el.viewer;                                                       // the full embed API: setVariant, setLights, exportVideo, …

Methods called before the scene has loaded wait for it. TypeScript: HTMLElementTagNameMap["verse-viewer"] is typed by verse-embed.d.ts (also shipped in @ctruhtech/verse-sdk).

React and Vue#

@ctruhtech/verse-react and @ctruhtech/verse-vue (in sdk/react, sdk/vue) are ~80-line wrappers with no dependencies beyond the framework: they load embed.js from your Verse origin once and render <verse-viewer>. Props mirror the attributes (camelCase; the element's load attribute is the loading prop), events arrive as callbacks / emits with the detail, and the ref exposes setCamera, playTour, stopTour, screenshot and viewer.

React#

Code
import { useRef } from "react";
import { VerseViewer } from "@ctruhtech/verse-react";

export function Listing({ sceneId }) {
  const viewer = useRef(null);
  return (
    <>
      <VerseViewer
        ref={viewer}
        host="https://verse.ctruh.com"
        src={sceneId}
        autoplayTour
        onLoad={(d) => console.log("loaded", d.name)}
        onViewChange={(d) => console.log(d.position)}
      />
      <button onClick={() => viewer.current.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] })}>Front view</button>
    </>
  );
}

Vue 3#

Code
<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";
import { VerseViewer } from "@ctruhtech/verse-vue";
const viewer = ref(null);
</script>

<template>
  <VerseViewer ref="viewer" host="https://verse.ctruh.com" :src="sceneId" autoplay-tour
    @load="(d) => console.log('loaded', d.name)" @view-change="(d) => console.log(d.position)" />
  <button @click="viewer.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] })">Front view</button>
</template>

No isCustomElement compiler option is needed: the wrapper renders the element itself.

Without a bundler: the Verse origin serves both wrappers at /sdk/react/index.js and /sdk/vue/index.js (CORS-enabled); map the framework with an import map. Complete pages are in the repository at sdk/examples/react.html and sdk/examples/vue.html.

The REST SDK#

@ctruhtech/verse-sdk — typed, dependency-free, ESM + CJS, Node 18+ and browsers. Without npm: import { VerseClient } from "https://verse.ctruh.com/sdk/verse-sdk.js".

Upload → ready → share#

Code
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { VerseClient } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";

const verse = new VerseClient({ baseUrl: "https://verse.ctruh.com", token: process.env.VERSE_TOKEN });

const bytes = await readFile("villa.glb");
const done = await verse.publish(bytes, {
  name: "palm-villa",
  resumable: true,                                   // chunked; survives a dropped connection
  onUploadProgress: (p) => console.log(`${Math.round(p.fraction * 100)} % uploaded`),
  onStage: (stage) => console.log("compiling:", stage), // preparing → queued → … → done
});
console.log(done.job, verse.shareLink(done));       // the scene id + its public link

publish() = upload() + waitForJob(); call them separately to store the job id and poll later (verse.job(id)). Failures throw VerseError with a friendly message and a stable code.

Publish settings#

Code
await verse.scenes.setVisibility(sceneId, "private");     // "public" | "unlisted" | "private"
await verse.scenes.setBackground(sceneId, "studio:warm");
await verse.scenes.setDefaultExperience(sceneId, expId); // the tour the link plays

Private links#

A private scene answers 404 to everyone but its owner and holders of a share token. One call mints a token and builds the link; revoking it kills that link (and every embed using it) and nothing else:

Code
const link = await verse.scenes.shares.link(sceneId);      // { id, shareToken, url, … } — token shown once
sendToClient(link.url);
// later
await verse.scenes.shares.revoke(sceneId, link.id);

Embed code#

Code
const { element, iframe, url } = verse.embedCode(sceneId, { share: link.shareToken, autoplayTour: true });
// element: <script src=".../embed.js" async></script>\n<verse-viewer src="…" share="…" autoplay-tour></verse-viewer>
// iframe:  a responsive lazy iframe (for CMSs that strip scripts)
const oe = await verse.oembed(verse.shareLink(sceneId)); // what WordPress / Notion / Slack fetch

Analytics#

Code
const a = await verse.analytics.scene(sceneId, { days: 30 });
console.log(a.views, a.uniqueViewers, a.time.medianSeconds, a.funnel);
const all = await verse.analytics.account({ days: 90 });   // + all.scenes[]
const csv = await verse.analytics.sceneCsv(sceneId);       // for a spreadsheet

Webhooks#

Register a URL; Verse POSTs to it when a scene you own finishes.

Code
const hook = await verse.webhooks.create({
  url: "https://example.com/verse-hook",
  events: ["scene.ready", "scene.failed"],
});
saveSecret(hook.secret);           // shown ONCE
await verse.webhooks.test(hook.id); // a signed `ping`, right now
Eventdata
scene.ready{ job, scene, status: "done", url, vpkUrl?, stats? }
scene.failed{ job, scene, status: "error", error, code }
comment.added · version.promoted · config.changedsee api.md § Webhooks
ping{ hook, events } — only from webhooks.test()

Each delivery is POST {id, event, t, account, data} with headers X-Verse-Event, X-Verse-Delivery, X-Verse-Timestamp and X-Verse-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")>. Answer any 2xx within 10 s. Anything else is retried — 3 tries, backoff 2 s then 8 s — and every attempt is in the delivery log (verse.webhooks.deliveries(hook.id), last 50). Hooks and logs persist with the rest of the server state (.verse-webhooks.json on the volume); ten hooks per account.

Receiver (Node, Express)#

Verify against the raw bytes, before parsing:

Code
import express from "express";
import { verifyWebhook } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";

const app = express();
app.post("/verse-hook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), async (req, res) => {
  const ok = await verifyWebhook({
    secret: process.env.VERSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
    body: req.body,                                   // Buffer
    signature: req.get("X-Verse-Signature"),
    timestamp: req.get("X-Verse-Timestamp"),          // older than 5 min → false
  });
  if (!ok) return res.sendStatus(401);
  const { event, data } = JSON.parse(req.body.toString("utf8"));
  if (event === "scene.ready") await markListingLive(data.scene, data.url);
  res.sendStatus(204);
});

Deliveries can repeat (a retry after a slow 2xx): dedupe on X-Verse-Delivery.

Receiver (any language)#

Code
import hmac, hashlib, time
def verify(secret: str, raw: bytes, sig: str, ts: str) -> bool:
    if abs(time.time() - int(ts)) > 300: return False
    want = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), ts.encode() + b"." + raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(want, sig or "")

Proof#

web/test/fix-verify-devkit.mjs runs all of the above against a real server: the element on tier A and tier C in a plain page on another origin (lazy, responsive, scroll guard, private token, setCamera → view-change, screenshot, autoplay tour, hotspot, tap-to-load), the React and Vue example pages, the SDK from upload to revoked link, and a webhook receiver that fails once (retry, signature, delivery log).
